items.body:
GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer

GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this:

In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.

This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on Novembe

items.body: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to N times M integrations when evaluating N methods on M benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark.
